top_signals.title: Trump Extends Jones Act Waiver For Another 90 Days
top_signals.summary: President Donald Trump extended the Jones Act waiver for another 90 days on Friday, keeping foreign-flagged tankers eligible to move oil and other commodities between U.S. ports as the war with Iran continues to drive up fuel costs. The extension, confirmed by a White House official who spoke to Reuters, continues what is already the longest waiver in the shipping law's history. Foreign vessels will still need approval for individual voyages due to a restriction introduced in August after earlier blanket exemptions drew opposition from the domestic…

top_signals.title: Trump Heads to China for Talks With Xi and Putin
top_signals.summary: Bloomberg White House correspondent Jeff Mason tells Bloomberg This Weekend how the Trump administration responded to a nationwide FAA ground stop and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s push for $50 billion to modernize the US air traffic control system. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Mason also looks ahead to President Donald Trump’s Asia trip and a planned meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping as technology and AI remain in focus. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: U.S. Oil Rig Count Holds at 463 as Crude Output Hits Another Record
top_signals.summary: The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States fell this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Friday, with the total rig count in the US falling to 601, up 52 from this same time last year. The number of active oil rigs stayed the same at 463 during the latest reporting period, according to the data. This is 46 above this same time last year. top_signals.title: Hydropower generation in the Southwest fell to record lows this summer
top_signals.summary: Prolonged drought conditions affecting the Colorado River Basin led to record low hydropower generation this summer in the Southwestern electricity supply region, which includes Arizona, New Mexico, and small parts of Nevada and California. Hydropower generation from April through August 2026 was 19% lower than during the same period last year and 28% lower than the 10-year average, according to the latest data from our Form EIA-923 survey
